prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting network scored 0.000 on both seeds. Training slid into pressing DONE at once: by the end, episodes were 1.0 step long, and at test time it placed nothing on 100% of designs. The likely cause is the hidden rule. The target, missing, extra and target-height channels are shifted 4 columns and wrap around, so the 3x3 convolutions cannot match a build cell with its target cell. Placements that follow the visible 'missing' cells land in the wrong spot and lose reward, so DONE looks best. The fix to test is a learned layer that covers a whole row or column with wraparound. A wraparound convolution whose kernel spans the full row can learn a shift that holds at every position, and it is not hard-coded to this grid. Entropy is raised to slow the slide into DONE. Each trial runs only about 20-90 updates, so a recipe with smaller, more frequent updates is worth one trial. With no wins yet, all three candidates aim to break out of zero.

### Round 2
Lining up the shifted target was the main obstacle. r1c1's wraparound full-row and full-column convolutions got 0.19, against 0 for the starting architecture, and almost no cells were placed outside the target. Two things still limit it:
(1) Collapse to DONE. r1c1 seed 0 nearly collapsed (mean episode length 2.0 at 25% of training), r1c2 dipped to 1.2, and r1c3 collapsed completely. The two seeds scored 0.08 and 0.31, so seed luck in escaping DONE drives most of the noise.
(2) Builds stop after layer 0. Both traces place only ground-layer bricks and then press DONE, and training success was still rising at the end, so the run is short of samples.
Two ideas follow. First, a cheap learned shift kernel shared across channels, which re-aligns the target channels cell by cell with the build. Stacking then becomes a local comparison. Second, a higher entropy bonus to resist DONE collapse. A cheaper network with fewer epochs gives more samples and should help with the stalled learning.

### Round 3
Removing the axial convolutions gave the biggest gain. r2c3 (cheap shift-align stem, 3 PPO epochs, entropy 0.03) scored 0.47 (0.55 and 0.38), against 0.19 for r1c1. Its seed-0 training success was still rising fast at the end (0.24 at 75%, 0.385 at 100%) and dev IoU was 0.93, so the agent finds the right cells and the limit looks like training samples, not capacity. Entropy 0.04 beat 0.02 on both seeds (r2c2 0.32 vs r1c1 0.19). Every run first drifts toward DONE (episode length about 2 at 25%). r1c3, with 2 epochs, small batches (128 worlds) and entropy 0.02, never escaped. So buying samples with fewer epochs should keep 256 worlds and a strong entropy bonus. This round: two single-change refinements of r2c3 (entropy 0.04; 2 epochs) and one push to the most samples (narrower network costing about the starting compute, plus 2 epochs and entropy 0.04).

### Round 4
The cheap learned shift-align module beats the costly axial convolutions. Spending compute on samples rather than width helps: the slim r3c3 reached 0.71 on one seed with IoU 0.95. The main risk is the early drift toward DONE. Mean episode length at 25% of training is about 2, and it fully collapsed in r1c3 and r3c2 seed 0 (both 2 epochs or tiny batches). The slim 2-epoch run r3c3 also had one weak seed (0.19). Every 3-epoch run kept both seeds alive (0.55/0.38, 0.47/0.32). Entropy between 0.03 and 0.04 makes no difference within noise. So: (A) the slim net with the more reliable 3 epochs, which still gets about 168k steps; (B) the slim net with 2 epochs and zero-initialised policy and value outputs, so it starts from a uniform policy and does not depend on random output-layer init; (C) both, zero-init plus 3 epochs.

## Trial it ended with
name: slim aligned net, 3 epochs
hypothesis: This is r3c3's slim network (compute about 1x the start) with 3 PPO epochs instead of 2. That gives about 168k steps, more than r2c3's 139k. Every 3-epoch run so far kept both seeds learning, while 2-epoch runs collapsed or stalled on one seed. So this should keep r3c3's sample advantage and lift the weak seed. Refuted if the mean is at or below r2c3's 0.47, or if one seed is still under 0.25.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: Round 1 states the rule outright: "The target, missing, extra and target-height channels are shifted 4 columns and wrap around, so the 3x3 convolutions cannot match a build cell with its target cell." This names the channels that changed, the 4-column shift and the wraparound. It doesn't say the shift goes toward higher x, but it captures what the rule changes and how. Later rounds build on this with "shift-align" modules.
